fact_text: The Strait of Hormuz crisis began on 28 Feb 2026 and the strait closed within one day of its start.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: About 15 to 20% of global oil supply passes through the Strait of Hormuz, as the interviewee stated.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: About 90 to 95% of Pakistan's crude imports were said to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, making the closure critical for the country.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Pakistan imports about 60 to 70% of its petrol and about 30% of its diesel, and most petrol imports come via the Gulf region.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: During the crisis, diesel exporters including Kuwait, Pakistan's main diesel supplier, stopped exporting, leaving diesel almost unavailable locally.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Pakistan has no strategic petroleum reserve; its fuel stock cover is commercial stock held by refineries and oil marketing companies.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Global oil prices rose about 40% after the crisis began on 28 Feb 2026, according to the reporter's opening remarks.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: The Dubai/Oman crude benchmark averaged about $127 a barrel in March 2026, a sharp rise on pre-crisis levels.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: The reporter said Pakistani consumers bore fuel costs up to 60% higher during the crisis, with pump prices changing weekly.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: India's retail fuel prices were reported unchanged since May 2022, as state-owned oil companies (about 75 to 80% of the market) and a price stabilisation fund absorb shocks.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: The interviewee said Pakistan's Ministry of Energy convened a meeting within minutes and hours of the crisis and formulated a response, which he called unusually fast.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: The Ministry of Energy, foreign affairs, civil and defence leadership, PNSC and the Navy helped bring cargoes out of the Strait, according to the interviewee.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Government permissions granted within days allowed some export-bound crude and condensate cargoes to be diverted back to refineries.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Crude from the Gulf was rerouted via a Red Sea route from Yanbu; one-way voyage time rose to about 8 to 10 days from about 4 to 5 days through the Strait.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Freight, insurance and war-risk premiums rose about 10 times during the crisis, raising the landed cost of imported crude.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: A refinery's gross refining margin depends mainly on the landed crude cost, which includes freight, insurance and customs duty, set against the product price.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Heavier crude yields more furnace oil than lighter crude, and refineries prefer lighter crude for petrol and diesel output; heavier grades were the only ones available from the region.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Some refineries trialled spot cargoes of African crude and US WTI, and the industry is working to add regional and mixed crudes to reduce Middle East dependence.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Crude purchases are planned about two months ahead under term contracts, so a temporary sanctions relief, such as on Russian crude, could not be used quickly.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: NRL's main term crude supplier is Aramco, whose Gulf cargoes were cut off; NRL switched to Red Sea-route cargoes from Yanbu, and its ADNOC term arrangement had lapsed and is being revived.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Furnace oil had been about 20 to 30% of domestic use, mainly for power, before LNG displaced it; the 2025 petroleum levy and carbon support levy cut domestic consumption to nearly zero.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Since the 2025 levies, about 100% of furnace oil sales are exported, up from 70 to 80% before, as domestic consumption has almost stopped.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Euro-5 refers to petrol and diesel quality, mainly cutting sulphur to 10 ppm; it is a separate policy question from the furnace oil glut.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Pakistan's brownfield refinery upgrade policy has been in the works for about six years, held up by tax changes until the government pushed it again in 2026.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: The brownfield policy incentive is reported to cover 27.5% of upgrade project costs over about six years, with refineries funding the rest through equity and debt.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: On a $2 billion upgrade, a refinery would still need about $1.4 to 1.5 billion after the 27.5% incentive, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: The five refineries together have about $6 billion of brownfield upgrade investment planned; some single projects are about $1.2 billion.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Petroleum products moved from zero-rated to exempt for sales tax, so refineries can no longer offset input sales tax against output, which became a major cost.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Refineries asked that sales tax on upgrade projects and machinery be waived from the 18% rate, and the government agreed in principle to work toward it.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: The government is reviewing whether to exempt the industry from sales tax or to zero-rate petroleum products, with an outcome possibly in the upcoming budget.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: A refinery upgrade takes about six years in total: feasibility and front-end design, licensing, EPC tender, financial close, then three to four years of EPC construction.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Upgrade technologies are licensed, so refineries buy technology packages from licensors before front-end engineering design, which is part of the early work.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Final investment decisions on refinery upgrades were held up until the policy and tax issues were resolved, and refineries signalled they would sign the policy together.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Producing petrol and diesel locally from furnace oil could replace about $1.5 to 2 billion of imports, the interviewee estimated.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Upgrade goals are Euro-5 diesel, Euro-5 petrol and lower furnace oil output; the interviewee said diesel imports could be cut close to 100%.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Refineries are pursuing energy efficiency and daytime solar pilots, and cleaner 10 ppm sulphur fuels, to cut energy use and their carbon footprint.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: NRL posted a profit in 2026 after losses in earlier quarters, which management credited to asset integrity programmes and reliability gains.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: NRL's asset integrity programme combines preventive maintenance and risk-based inspection, which the CEO said lifted plant reliability to target levels.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: NRL's sales rose about 25 to 30% year on year in 2026, after reliability gains let it guarantee supply.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: The number of oil marketing companies has grown to about 42 from three large ones, making it a buyers' market that refineries must work to serve.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Management said that in a buyers' market a refinery must engage OMCs, build relationships and provide customer service, not rely on technical reliability alone.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Rising crude prices give refineries inventory gains, which reverse as prices fall, so the later inventory loss is expected to be about as significant.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Diesel margins spiked during the shortage because diesel could not reach the market, and refinery gross margins stayed positive in March 2026.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Without imports by refineries and OMCs, national fuel stocks could have run out within 10 to 20 days, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: A fuel shortage in Pakistan quickly becomes a law and order risk at pumps, as queues form when prices change or stocks fall.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Dubai/Oman crude reached a high of $167 per barrel in March 2026 and averaged about $127 per barrel, after the crisis began on 28 Feb 2026.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: On diesel the current margin is 7.5% plus a deemed duty incentive, bringing the total to 10%, and the speaker said 2.5 percentage points would go into an escrow account.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)

fact_text: Pakistan exports furnace oil at a loss; converting it into petrol and diesel at home would substitute about USD 1.52 billion of imports, the speaker said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'What's Delaying Refinery Upgrades? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-06-02)
